title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Healthcare Assistant Days or Nights Luxury Retirement Home AV2073 A

Location: Doncaster
Pay: £31,948.80 per annum
Hours: Full Time Days or Nights

About the Home

We are recruiting on behalf of a privately owned residential care home in Doncaster, providing a welcoming and supportive environment for 11 residents.

This small, friendly home offers a personalised approach to care, ensuring residents receive the support they need while maintaining their dignity, independence and choice. With a focus on individual needs and wellbeing, the home aims to create a comfortable and homely atmosphere where residents feel safe, valued and respected.

Working within a smaller care setting offers the opportunity to build meaningful relationships with residents and colleagues, helping to create a positive and supportive community.

The Role

As a Healthcare Assistant, you will play an important role in delivering high-quality, person-centred care and supporting residents with their daily living needs. You will work as part of a dedicated team to ensure residents receive compassionate support in a safe, comfortable and respectful environment.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing compassionate care and support to residents.
- Assisting with personal care and daily living activities.
- Supporting residents with mobility, comfort and general wellbeing.
- Building positive relationships with residents and their families.
- Promoting dignity, independence and choice at all times.
- Supporting residents with meals, hydration and social activities.
- Maintaining accurate care records and reporting any concerns.
- Following care plans and adhering to health and safety procedures.

About You
- Minimum of six months' experience within a care setting.
- A caring, compassionate and reliable approach.
- Strong communication and teamwork skills.
- A genuine passion for supporting people with their care needs.
- Ability to deliver person-centred care with dignity and respect.
- Willingness to learn and develop within the role.

Benefits & Perks
- £31,948.80 per annum.
- Full-time day or night shifts.
- Opportunity to work within a small, privately owned care home.
- Supportive team environment.
- Ongoing training and development opportunities.
- The opportunity to build meaningful relationships with residents.
- A rewarding role with opportunities to develop your care career.

To Apply

title: Support Worker
company: CRP Group Global Ltd - Agency - Temporary
description:
We are currently recruiting for a Housing Support Worker to join an organization in Doncaster. This is a temporary, full-time opportunity with the potential to become permanent for the right person.

The service supports young people living in social housing who may be experiencing issues / challenges that can affect their ability to maintain stable accommodation and live independently.

The Role

As a Housing Support Worker, you will provide practical and emotional support to residents, helping them maintain their accommodation, develop independent living skills and access appropriate support services.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing one-to-one support to residents within a supported housing environment
- Building positive, professional relationships with residents
- Supporting individuals experiencing drug and/or alcohol misuse
- Helping residents maintain their tenancy and accommodation
- Identifying and responding appropriately to safeguarding concerns
- Supporting residents to access health, welfare and specialist support services
- Encouraging independent living and positive lifestyle choices
- Helping residents work towards individual support plans and personal goals
- Maintaining accurate and confidential records
- Liaising with external agencies and support providers where required
- Promoting a safe, respectful and supportive environment for all residents

About You

We are looking for someone who is compassionate, resilient and confident working with young adults.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in a Housing Support Worker, Support Worker, Hostel Worker, Recovery Worker, Outreach Worker or similar role
- Experience supporting people affected by drug and/or alcohol misuse
- An understanding of safeguarding and professional boundaries
- Good communication and interpersonal skills
- The ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations
- A genuine commitment to helping people improve their circumstances
- The ability to work independently as well as part of a wider support team
